title: Pattern vs Outlier
summary: Pattern = plan for it; Outlier = understand it first — do not base strategy on a single point.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **Not** every **strange number** deserves a **change in your plan** — you need to know: **Is this a recurring pattern** or an **exception for one time**?
- **Why now?** In the previous lesson, you **extracted summaries** from **AI (artificial intelligence)**. Now you need to **distinguish** what **requires a decision** and what **only needs an explanation**.
- **What after the lesson?** You will classify **5 numbers or days**: **Pattern**, **Exception**, or **Not enough data**.

sections.heading: Tension — One strange number — and I decided to change everything
sections.subtitle: One strange number — and I decided to change everything
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **One day**, sales **tripled** — so I decided to **double the ads**. **The following week**, they returned to **normal**.
- The problem: A **strategic decision** was made based on an **exception**. A **one-time campaign**, a **big client**, or a **recording error** — does **not necessarily** mean a **new system**.
- **Before** you act on **one number** — ask: **Has this happened before?** Or is it the **first time**?

sections.heading: Core idea — Pattern = plan — Exception = understand
sections.subtitle: Pattern = plan — Exception = understand
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Pattern:** Something that **repeats** over **different periods** — **deserves** to be **planned** for (budget, SOP, forecast).
- **Outlier:** Something that **happened once or twice** **away from the usual** — **understand its cause** before making **any major decision**.
- **Not enough data:** **One point** or **two days** — **do not make** a strategic decision. **Gather more** or **wait**.
- **Practical rule:** **3 times** in **3 different periods** = a **pattern** you can **trust**.

sections.heading: Glossary — Two terms to distinguish
sections.subtitle: Two terms to distinguish
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| **Pattern** | **Regular repetition** you can **expect** and **plan** for | Sales of **cakes** **double every Friday** for **6 months** |
| **Outlier** | **A number far** from the usual — **happened once or twice** only | **One day** I sold **50,000** and the average is **500** — due to a **bulk client** |

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** Your sales **every Friday** are **30–40% higher** than the other days — **for 3 months**. **Only one day** **quintupled** due to a **big client**. **What do you do?**

Double the ads** because of the **big client day**.**
**Plan to increase stock on Thursday** — because **Friday is a recurring pattern**.
Ignore** Friday and the big client — **both** are unimportant.**

**Explanation:** **Friday = pattern** — **deserves planning**. **Big client day = exception** — **understand it** but **do not build** your **strategy** on it.

sections.heading: Mission — Classify 5 numbers or days
sections.subtitle: Classify 5 numbers or days
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** A **practical distinguishing** mission — **not** a graph. Take **5 numbers or 5 days** from your **work** (real or imagined) and **classify** each one. **Goal:** You learn to **pause** before you **change a decision** because of a **strange number**.

**Delivery:**

1. The **Metric** you track (sales, orders, complaints…)
2. **5 values** — each on a line (number + day/week)
3. For each value: **Pattern / Exception / Not enough data + why**
4. **One decision** you will make **based on the pattern only** (**not** the exception)

**Evaluation criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Correct classification | 60% | Each value **classified** **for a clear reason**; **exceptions** **not treated** as a pattern |
| Decision from the pattern | 40% | The decision **based on repetition** — **not** on **one point** |

sections.heading: Confidence close
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **I understood:** **Not** every **strange number** deserves a **change in your plan**. The **pattern** deserves a **decision** — the **exception** deserves an **explanation**.
- **You can:** **Pause** and ask, “**Does this repeat?**” before **any strategic decision**.
- **Next:** **Decision rule** — **one number** may **mislead you**; the decision needs **comparison** and **related numbers**.
